scope.anatomy: Paired left precentral (M1) and postcentral (S1) gyri shown as coronal-orientation cut faces in the existing Finger Pathway Atlas coordinate system.
scope.layers: Six isocortical layers are present in both sections. M1 is modeled as agranular with a very thin or indistinct layer IV and expanded pyramidal layers; S1 is modeled as granular with a prominent thalamorecipient layer IV.
scope.microstructure: Twelve H01 source neurite components with original object IDs and source-layer labels are transplanted rigidly to both M1/S1 samples. H01 is temporal cortex. Remaining cells and glial context are representative models; positions, new axon continuations and region assignments are not measured M1/S1 tissue or mapped synapses.
scope.tracts: No DKI acquisition has been fitted. Primary DKI references provide a proposed workflow for voxel-scale orientation peaks and anatomical tracking. Rendered individual axon cylinders, spacing, radii and endpoints are modeled; these are not DKI-derived observations.
scope.mri: MRI-style illustrative coronal tissue sections at two separate anterior-posterior planes, not a patient MRI, a segmented scan, or a single slice placing M1 and S1 side by side.

m1.label: Primary motor cortex / precentral gyrus
m1.specialization: Agranular cortex; layer IV is retained as a thin six-layer bookkeeping band rather than claimed as a sharply defined granular layer. Layer V has the largest representative corticofugal somata.

s1.label: Primary somatosensory cortex / postcentral gyrus
s1.specialization: Granular cortex; layer IV is expanded as the principal thalamorecipient band.

lod.gross: Only the left source precentral and postcentral gyri are rendered in the body view.
lod.laminar: Two separate coronal cameras keep all six layers of both samples visible at the same physical magnification.
lod.cellular: 620 distinct sample cells, including 24 transplanted instances of twelve H01 source trees, connected cylindrical arbors and projection continuations.
lod.visibilityNote: Source and cell radii remain physical; optional axonal radius padding improves visibility. Counts and spacing are representative, not stereological measurements.

dkiRules: Use local orientation-distribution peaks and cortical surface normals as direction priors.
Render multiple nearby streamlines as an uncertainty envelope rather than a single asserted tract.
Terminate thalamocortical orientation families preferentially in S1 layer IV and originate corticofugal families preferentially in M1 layer V.
Include short association U-fiber orientation under the central-sulcus interval.
Do not infer axon identity, synapse identity, conduction direction or exact endpoints from DKI alone.
implementation.dkiRulesStatus: Proposed modeling guidance, not a fitted diffusion-data result.
